spec.name: Earnings drift v4
spec.notes: Searched 253 variants of this signal; the figure quoted is the best of them and should be read with that in mind. The family has a long record as a premium.

claim.text: Research-period backtest: Sharpe 2.0, annual return 7%, maximum drawdown 4%.

exhibits.summary: The log holds 254 distinct specs; the best of 254 under no edge is expected to reach a Sharpe of 0.55, so the claimed 2.00 becomes 1.45 and the probability that the true Sharpe is above zero is 100%.
On the sealed period, traded as live (strict data, 10 bps, at least one bar of lag), the Sharpe ratio is 2.46 against 2.02 in research, a gap of -0.44.
The real signal's gross Sharpe of 2.17 beats 100% of 200 shuffled signals (shuffled mean 0.03, 95th percentile 0.63).
Delaying the signal by 1 more bar moves the Sharpe ratio from 2.02 to 1.96 (change -0.06).
On the full universe the Sharpe ratio is 2.02 against 2.02 as submitted; the strategy never saw 0 delisted assets.
The scan (a heuristic) found no phrase addressed to reviewers or giving instructions in 2 text sources.

verdict.opinion: The strategy's claimed Sharpe ratio of 2.0 is significantly inflated. EX-1 shows that the best of 254 variants is expected to have a Sharpe of 0.55, but the claimed 2.0 is adjusted to 1.45. This suggests the performance is not real, warranting paper trading only.
